title: Find Good Days to Rob the Bank
notes:
## Intuition

Checking the `time` days on each side of every day costs O(n · time). Instead, notice that a window never goes up exactly when none of its day-to-day steps is a rise. Counting rises with prefix sums answers "how many rises are inside this window?" in O(1), and the same works for falls on the right side.

## Approach

1. Build `rises[i]`: how many of the steps from day 0 up to day `i` go up (`security[k] > security[k - 1]`). Build `falls[i]` the same way for steps that go down.
2. Only days `i` with `i >= time` and `i + time < n` have enough days on both sides, so loop over exactly those.
3. The steps inside the left window are the ones into days `i - time + 1` to `i`; it has no rise when `rises[i] - rises[i - time]` is `0`.
4. The right window's steps go into days `i + 1` to `i + time`; it has no fall when `falls[i + time] - falls[i]` is `0`.
5. When both hold, add `i` to `days`.

## Example 1, step by step

`security = [5, 3, 3, 3, 5, 6, 2]`, `time = 2`. The steps are fall, flat, flat, rise, rise, fall, so `rises = [0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 2, 2]` and `falls = [0, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 2]`. Candidates are days 2 to 4. Day 2: `rises[2] - rises[0] = 0` and `falls[4] - falls[2] = 0`, good. Day 3: `0` and `falls[5] - falls[3] = 0`, good. Day 4: `rises[4] - rises[2] = 1`, not good. The answer is `[2, 3]`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): one pass builds both prefix arrays and one pass checks the days.
- Space: O(n) for `rises` and `falls`.

## Pitfalls

- Equal neighbours are allowed on both sides; count only strict rises and strict falls.
- `time` can exceed half the array; the loop bounds then make the answer empty without reading outside the array.
- With `time = 0` every day is good, and the loop covers all of them.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `n` | number of days |
| `rises[i]` | steps going up among the steps into days `1..i` |
| `falls[i]` | steps going down among the steps into days `1..i` |
| `days` | the good days found |
| `noRiseBefore`, `noFallAfter` | whether each window has the required shape |

narration.3: rises[i] will count the upward steps among days 0..i.
narration.4: falls[i] will count the downward steps among days 0..i.
narration.5: Walk through every step from day i - 1 to day i.
narration.6: Carry the count forward and add one if guards went up on this step.
narration.7: Carry the count forward and add one if guards went down on this step.
narration.10: Only days with at least time days on both sides can be good.
narration.11: The window before day i must contain no upward step.
narration.12: The window after day i must contain no downward step.
narration.13: Both windows have the right shape...
narration.14: ...so day i is a good day.
narration.17: Return every good day found, in increasing order.
